concept.name: Midpoint
concept.definition: The arithmetic mean of the best bid and best offer, conventionally computed from the NBBO; Regulation NMS uses the NBBO midpoint as the reference price for effective and realized spread calculations. It is the standard benchmark for the unobserved transaction-cost-free value of a security between trades.
concept.intuition: It is the neutral point splitting the spread - neither side's concession - so it serves as the default fair-value reference for measuring execution quality.
concept.mechanics: Recomputed on every change to the best bid or offer; used as the peg for midpoint orders, as the benchmark in spread and price-improvement statistics, and as the reference in trade-classification rules such as the quote rule.
concept.formula: M = (B + A) / 2, where B is the best (national best) bid and A the best (national best) offer.
concept.failure_modes: When the spread is wide, one side is thin, or prices are tick-constrained, the midpoint is a poor value estimate; it also ignores the size imbalance between bid and ask, which the microprice corrects.
concept.misconceptions: The midpoint is a benchmark, not a tradable price and not necessarily the market's true valuation; executions at the midpoint are a convention, not a law.
concept.example: With the NBBO at $100.00 x $100.04, the midpoint is $100.02; a buy executed at $100.03 shows $0.02 of effective spread (2 x (100.03 - 100.02)).
